solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: These may be raised by good girls

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
lasses are young women, a northern and Scottish word for girls

explanation.surface: Well-behaved girls being praised or lifted up by admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' suggests children being brought up, but the things raised are drinking vessels lifted in a toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking vessels are lifted together when people make a toast or celebrate, so they are things that get raised.

clue.text: Looks at candy around noon with son

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for candy encloses the letter for noon

parts.note: glacé means candied, as in glacé cherries
N is the abbreviation for noon
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A boy eyes up sweets at midday with his son in tow.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief quick peeks, or the verb peeks quickly, are synonyms for quick looks.

clue.text: Love a party with budget

parts.note: taken as written
a do is an informal word for a party
to budget something is to ration it; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: Romance blossoms at a celebration held on a tight budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep devotion or worship of someone is an intense form of affection.

clue.text: Mister, for example, holding present

indicators.note: holding means clutching inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: say means for example, as in fruit, say an apple
pr is a dictionary abbreviation for present

explanation.surface: A man, for instance, clutching a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister' looks like a title for a man but is the device that produces a fine mist.
explanation.definitionFit: A mister is a device producing a fine jet of liquid droplets, so it is an atomiser or sprinkler.

clue.text: New dates held up by rash firm

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
fast can mean reckless or rash, as in fast living

explanation.surface: New romantic dates delayed because of a skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'held up by' puts the first part above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolute and unwavering, a loyal friend or steady commitment is called firm in this sense.

clue.text: Brat with oil ruined ring road

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked out of its proper shape, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
'with' joins the word oil to the fodder

explanation.surface: A spoilt child pours oil all over a motorway and wrecks it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a road circling a city, such as the M25 around London, is called an orbital, a noun use.

clue.text: Curses open-topped vessels, hard to be inside

indicators.note: to be inside means placed within, so the letter for hard goes in
open-topped means with the top removed, which in a down clue is the first letter

parts.note: boats are vessels
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone swears at boats without decks while trying to stay in.
explanation.definitionFit: Swear words and profanities are also called by this name, alongside the sense of solemn promises.

clue.text: Who shouts about rising leak? One who serves

indicators.note: about means around, so the shouter goes around the other piece

parts.note: a barker shouts to draw crowds at a fair

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means going upwards, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a leak is slang for urinating

explanation.surface: A question about who is yelling about water coming up, then a server.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs a pub or pours drinks behind the bar serves customers.

clue.text: Tribute for a street

parts.note: to can mean for, as in a gift to a friend
taken as written
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A memorial honouring a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses and drinking to someone's health is a tribute paid at a celebration.

clue.text: In every other place Enigma fills image of the distant past

definitions.note: the answer is an adverbial phrase, the definition a noun phrase

indicators.note: fills means goes into, so those letters are put inside the word for image

parts.note: a logo is an image used as an emblem

indicators.note: every other place means alternate positions, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Enigma

explanation.surface: Wartime code-breaking machinery evokes images of a bygone age.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigma suggests the wartime cipher machine, but only its alternate letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happened in the distant past happened a great while back, many years before now.

clue.text: Romance is what shields when one Romeo is dumped

indicators.note: something dumped is thrown away, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: armour is protective covering that shields a body
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet; 'one' because only one of the two Rs goes

explanation.surface: A heartbroken lover drops their defences when Romeo leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for love is used in English for a love affair, especially a secret or passionate romantic liaison.

clue.text: Please introduce American packing bread

parts.note: to enter data is to introduce or put it in

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: a tin is a loaf baked in a tin, and also slang for money, which is bread too
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A polite request to bring in an American who is carrying a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please' looks like a polite opener but is the verb meaning delight.
explanation.definitionFit: To please people is to amuse or divert them, which is what an entertainer does for an audience.

clue.text: Whirlpool daily rejected by attractive woman, but not husband

parts.note: a char or daily is a British term for a cleaning woman who comes in each day

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the little word after it is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

indicators.note: 'but not' tells us to leave out the letter for husband

parts.note: a dish is slang for an attractive person
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A cleaning woman is turned away by a glamorous woman whose husband is absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word but is itself the fodder turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a deadly whirlpool opposite the monster Scylla in the Strait of Messina bore this name.

clue.text: Excessive former skill returned

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: returned means sent back the way it came, so the word for skill reads backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An old talent has come back far too strongly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something additional or surplus to what is needed is more than required, the adjective sense of superfluous.

clue.text: Small pet could be tiring

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a pet is a fit of sulking or pique, as is a tiff, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Looking after a little animal can be exhausting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an animal but is the old noun for a fit of bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A strenuous climb or test is described with this adjective, meaning hard work and demanding effort.

clue.text: Complete clues fall freely

indicators.note: freely means without constraint, so the letters can move into any order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finished crossword hints tumble out easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Full-scale means total, thorough and all-out, as in a full-scale inquiry, so it means complete.

clue.text: A new list regarding what gets meal going

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
to list is to lean or tip over, as a ship does
as to means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone drawing up a fresh list about how to start a dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter of cold meats, olives and vegetables served before the main courses opens the dinner.

clue.text: Pavarotti's sign of course cut short

indicators.note: cut short means docked at the end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the tenor of something is its general course or drift
cleft means cut or split

explanation.surface: A singer's star sign, which of course is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' hints at the zodiac, but it is a musical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Pavarotti was a tenor, and the musical symbol placing middle C for his voice range on a stave bears that name.

clue.text: Developing and flowering in season

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: spring is a season
flowers that are out are in bloom

explanation.surface: Plants growing and blooming during a time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoots or buds begin to grow from a plant when it starts to develop, the literal and figurative sense.

clue.text: Bachelor, say, to confess and squeal

parts.note: to sing is criminal slang for confessing to the police
to let on is to reveal a secret, which is what a squealer does

explanation.surface: An unmarried man is urged to own up and blab.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who is unmarried or unattached is so called, and a bachelor is one example of such a person.

clue.text: Release kit without cost

parts.note: a set is a collection of equipment, a kit
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: An advert offers to hand over equipment at no charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate a prisoner or captive animal is to let them go, giving them liberty.

clue.text: Countryside river, one in Russia

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
the Ural is a river in Russia, so 'one' means another river

explanation.surface: A scenic waterway flowing through Russian countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside is used attributively, as in countryside pursuits, meaning belonging to the country rather than the town.

clue.text: Perhaps flier in meadow left awkwardly

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily, so the letters are jumbled into an odd order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Maybe a bird, left clumsily in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a bird or pilot, but it is a printed handout.
explanation.definitionFit: A flier (or flyer) is a printed handbill, and a folded printed handout is one example of that.

clue.text: Carbon-capture machines are commonly in fixed returns

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
returns means goes back, so the word for fixed is read backwards

parts.note: set means fixed or firm
're is the casual contracted form of are, as in they're

explanation.surface: Pollution-fighting devices are usually locked into returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Machines' suggests engineering, but the definition is playful: plants absorb carbon dioxide naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody plants absorb carbon dioxide from the air and lock it into their wood, so they act like natural capture devices.

clue.text: Clear air continuously losing a degree of insulation?

indicators.note: losing means giving something up, so those letters are removed

parts.note: together can mean without a break, as in for days together
a tog is a unit measuring the warmth or insulation of duvets

explanation.surface: Clean air keeps leaking away the warmth of the insulation.
explanation.walkthrough: A tog is the British unit used to rate how warm a duvet is.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetically the clear upper sky or heavens, the pure air above the clouds, is given this name.

clue.text: Spider is otherwise a natural source of trepidation

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of trepidation

explanation.surface: A spider is, unsurprisingly, something that naturally frightens people.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy spider of the family Theraphosidae, named after Taranto in Italy, is called this.

clue.text: Telly Savalas's third to appear in upcoming trial

indicators.note: upcoming in a down clue means going up, so the word reads bottom to top
to appear in means placed inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: third points to the letter in the third position of the word

parts.note: the third letter of Savalas

explanation.surface: Telly Savalas is set to feature in a forthcoming court case.
explanation.walkthrough: Telly Savalas was the actor who played Kojak; here 'Telly' is just the British word for television.
explanation.definitionFit: Telly is British informal for television, and the receiving apparatus is the physical box in the sitting room.

clue.text: Suitable position found in hotel in French city

indicators.note: found in means located within, so the letter for hotel goes inside the city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
hotel is H in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A good spot discovered in a hotel on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A role or place exactly suited to someone, as in finding one's niche in life, is an apt spot.

clue.text: Honest about catches? Practice

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for honest goes round the other piece

parts.note: real means genuine or honest
to catch what someone says is to hear it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an honest person is really making those catches, then says it's only practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance of a play or concert, run through before the real thing, is practice for it.

clue.text: Sudden fear as Charlie fell

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
a fell is a hill or upland moor in northern England

explanation.surface: Panic struck when Charlie tumbled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as the past tense of fall, but it is the northern English noun for a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiver of sudden alarm or dread, as in a chill ran down my spine, is a sudden fear.

clue.text: Draw in France is impassioned

parts.note: to draw a salary is to earn it
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A tied match in France is a heated affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sincere and intensely serious in their feeling or conviction is described with this adjective.

clue.text: On getting into scrap goods to be shifted

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a scrap is a brawl or fight
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone gets dragged into a brawl over merchandise that needs moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests junk to be shifted, but it means a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo carried by lorry, ship, train or plane is the commercial load transported from place to place.
